assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframed intracellular organization as liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent biomolecules, bringing phase-behaviour thinking (demixing, thermodynamic driving forces, interfaces) into cell biology. A genuinely new concept of molecular organisation with broad reach into neurodegeneration and condensate biology; precisely the kind of physical chemistry of life I value.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granule liquid-like behaviour (2009), the founding observation; Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase-diagram work gave the quantitative physical-chemical framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence grammar and physics, so a three-person cut leaves excluded contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept widely adopted and independently reproduced over 15+ years, and clearly impactful. Active debate on which in-cell structures are truly phase separated and on functional significance, but the core physical principle is stable.
uncertainties: Extent to which in vivo condensates are equilibrium phases versus other assemblies is debated.
Fair division of credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved.
Some in vitro condensate claims have been criticised as artefacts; I rely on recalled knowledge, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly engineered for function: pH-dependent charge, phase behaviour and membrane fusion enabled efficient encapsulation and endosomal release of nucleic acids. The concrete societal impact (mRNA vaccines, siRNA drugs) is enormous, and the underlying lipid physical chemistry is central.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope, Madden and colleagues developed ionizable lipid formulation and rapid-mixing manufacture; MacLachlan and Anderson/Langer contributed lead lipids and optimisation for siRNA and mRNA. Credit is spread over several groups and industry, making a clean three-person allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is massive (siRNA drug approval, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines), though the 2023 Medicine prize went to nucleoside modification, so a Chemistry prize on the delivery vehicle is plausible and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine recognition may affect committee appetite.
Patent and industrial credit disputes complicate attribution.
Whether the committee views it as chemistry discovery versus formulation engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Directed self-assembly of discrete metal-ligand cages and polyhedra showed that thermodynamically controlled coordination equilibria give precise nanoscale hosts. Concept-forming for supramolecular chemistry, with applications in encapsulation, catalysis and stabilising reactive species.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (square and cage complexes, Pd-pyridyl assemblies), Stang (coordination-driven self-assembly of polygons and polyhedra) and Raymond (tetrahedral M4L6 hosts, confined catalysis) are the central founders; Nitschke and Ward are later major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation; the field is mature. However supramolecular chemistry was recognised in 1987 and 2016, which could weigh against it.
uncertainties: Real-world applications remain modest compared with the conceptual impact.
Dispute over relative priority among the three founders.
Prior Nobel recognition of related supramolecular and molecular machine work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and funnel theory recast protein folding as statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic navigation of a rugged landscape, resolving Levinthal's paradox and unifying folding, misfolding and aggregation. Deep physical-chemical principle with lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed funnel and minimal-frustration theory; Dill introduced hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model views; Fersht gave the experimental kinetic mapping. Who counts as decisive is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely accepted and experimentally supported, though AlphaFold (2024 prize) altered the context; some may see folding theory as already partly covered.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 recognition of structure prediction.
Theory-heavy with indirect experimental validation.
Allocation between theory and experiment (Fersht) is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers (thiols on gold) established molecularly defined, tunable surfaces and a platform for wetting, adhesion, biointerfaces and soft lithography. A clean example of interfacial self-assembly as a general principle.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiol and disulfide monolayers on gold (1983); Whitesides developed the systematic structure-property and patterning work. Sagiv's earlier silane monolayer work complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely used; recognition would be late but unquestionably impactful.
uncertainties: Priority questions involving Sagiv and Langmuir-Blodgett precedents.
Whitesides' breadth makes the decisive contribution harder to isolate.
Whether the committee sees this as a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and dynamics, enabling ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions such as water and proton transport. A foundational computational method used across chemistry and materials science.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is clearly the decisive contribution and a tidy two-laureate configuration. Parrinello also appears on metadynamics and ML potentials, which could allow a broader citation.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of validation, with entrenched use; recognition is highly mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Parrinello appears under several candidates, so how the committee would frame a joint prize is unclear.
Superseded in some uses by Born-Oppenheimer MD and ML potentials.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant liquid-crystal templating of mesoporous silica (MCM-41, SBA-15) applies lyotropic phase behaviour to produce ordered materials with tunable pores, directly a soft-matter self-assembly principle with wide use in catalysis, adsorption and delivery.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) made MCM-41; Ryoo, Stucky and Zhao extended to larger pores and diverse structures; Inagaki independently reported FSM-16. Industrial authorship and parallel discovery complicate selection.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation and extension; timely but with commercial impact smaller than the scientific influence.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery (Inagaki) and corporate priority.
Practical industrial impact is more limited than for zeolites.
Three-name selection leaves out major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites produced a spectacular rise in solution-processed solar cell efficiency, a remarkable materials chemistry story with deep defect-tolerance and ionic-electronic physical chemistry questions.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009); Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's meso-superstructured and thin-film devices were pivotal; Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also strong claimants, so allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Impact is high but stability, toxicity and commercial viability remain unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Long-term operational stability is not settled.
Contested credit among many contributors.
Maturity relative to other candidates is questionable.
